THE 82nd ANNUAL REPORT 
- of the - 
YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF MONTREAL 


For the year ending March 31st, 1933 


(« 


THE REPORT OF THE GENERAL SECRETARY 
OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION OF MONTREAL 
FOR THE YEAR ENDING MARCH 31st, 1933 


A_STRENUOUS YEAR: 


THE YEAR JUST CLOSED -= THE 82ND SINCE THE FOUNDING 
OF THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION == WELL LONG BE REMEMBERED IN 
ECONOMIC HISTORY AS ONE IN WHICH THE BUSINESS DEPRESSION 
REACHED EVEN LOWER LEVELS THAN IN 1931, WHICH, I(T WILL BE 
RECALLED, HAD THE REPUTATION OF BEING A "PANIC YEAR." 


THE YEAR WAS MARKED IN WORLD AFFAIRS BY THE ELECTION 
TO POWER BY AN OVERWHELMING MAJORITY OF THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY 
IN THE UNITEO STATES, ANO THE DEFAULT TO THEM BY FIVE NATIONS 
OF THEIR PAYMENTS ON ACCOUNT OF WAR DEBTS. THE MOST OUT- 
STANDING EVENT IN CANADIAN LIFE WAS THE IMPERIAL ECONOMIC 
CONFERENCE WHICH SAT AT OTTAWA IN JUNEe THIS MARKED THE 
BEGINNING OF AN ATTEMPT TO TRANSLATE A POLITICAL COMMONWEALTH 
OF NATIONS INTO AN ECONOM!C COMMONWEALTH AND TO USE IT AS A 
LEVER FOR LOWERING THE TARIFF WALLS OF THE WORLD. 


TYPICAL AMONG THE GREAT ECONOMIC PROBLEMS OF CANADA 
WERE THE PLIGHT OF OUR NEWSPRINT INDUSTRY, THE EXTREMELY 
DIFFICULT RAILWAY SITUATION, AND THE NEW ALL-TIME LOW PRICE 
OF WHEAT. 


BUE TO THIS LONG DRAWN OUT TRADE RECESSION, UNEM-~ 
PLOYMENT, WITH ALL ITS SERIOUSLY DISTURBING SOCIAL EFFECTS, 
HAS HELO ITS PLACE AS A MAJOR PROBLEM CONFRONTING OUR 
METROPOLITAN CITYe THERE HAS BEEN AN APPALLING AMOUNT OF 
UNHAPPINESS AND EVEN RUIN IN MANY OIRECTLONS, AND THE YOUNG 
MEN AND BOYS, WHO CONSTITUTE THE ASSOCIATION'S MAIN 
CONSTITUENCY, HAVE SUFFERED THEIR FULL SHAREs QUITE ASIDE 
FROM THE ABNORMAL NUMBER OF SUICIDES UNDER THESE CONDITIONS, 
THERE ARE SERIOUS CONSEQUENCES ACCRUING TO THE INDIVIDUAL 
WHO 1S UNABLE TO EARN HIS LIVELIHOOD. EXPERTS IN THE FIELD 
OF MENTAL HYGIENE TELL US, FOR EXAMPLE, THAT MEN IN THIS 
PLIGHT FREQUENTLY BECOME HYPER-SENSITIVE AND UNDULY 
SUSCEPTIBLE TO SLIGHTS AND MISUNDERSTANDINGS, OR DEVELOP 
DELUSIONS OF PERSECUTION, OR THEY MAY SEEK TO EVADE THE 
ISSUES CONFRONTING THEM BY SELF-DECEPTION AND DAY DREAMING, 
AND THAT EVEN THE LEAST-AFFECTED MAY OEVELOP FEELINGS OF 
INFERIORITY AND LOSE CONFIOENCE IN THEMSELVES. 


FOR THE YOUNGER 'GENERATION, THE SITUATION HAS BEEN 
EQUALLY SERIOUSe GRADUATION FROM SCHOOL OR COLLEGE, UNDER 
THESE CONDITIONS, DOES NOT LEAD TO CREATIVE OPPORTUNITY 
BUT RATHER TO°AIMLESS IDLENESS. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO 
MEASURE THE -DAMAGE DONE TO -A°GENERATION OF YOUTH BY THIS 
SENSE OF FRUSTRATION AND DISAPPOINTMENTe THE RESULT IS NOT 
ONLY AN IRREPARASLE LOSS TO THE INDIVIDUAL BUT ALSO AN 
INCALCULABLE LOSS TO THE WHOLE COMMUNITY. 


IT SHOULD BE POINTED OUT THAT, TO AN EXTRAORDINARY 
DEGREE, THESE YOUNG MEN AND 8OYS, WHILE BEARING SO LARGE A 
SHARE OF THE BRUNT OF THIS SITUATION HAVE ENDURED THEIR 
PLIGHT PHILOSOPHICALLY ANO HAVE FACED THESE UNPRECEDENTED 
DIFFICULTIES IN A MOST CREDITABLE SPIRITe THE YeMeCeAc 
HAS PLAYED A WORTHY PART IN MAINTAINING THEIR MORALS, AND 
OUR SUBSCRIBERS TO THE EXPANSION CAMPAIGN OF 1928 SHOULD 
REALIZE THAT MUCH THAT HAS BEEN ACCOMPLISHED WOULD HAVE 
BEEN QUITE IMPOSSIBLE WITHOUT THE FACILITIES MADE POSSIBLE 
BY THE BUILDING PROGRAM OF 1929 AND 1930. 


IN ITS EFFORT TO RENDER A LARGE VOLUME OF SERVICES 
TO THE UNEMPLOYED, THE ASSOCIATION HAS, IN COMMON WITH OTHER 
VOLUNTEER AGENCIES, FACED _A SITUATION OF CONSIDERABLE GRAVITY. 
THAT IT HAS THUS FAR SURVIVED THE HEAVY GALES OF THESE TRYING 
TIMES IS A TRIBUTE TO ITS VITALITY AND THE NEED FOR ITS 
SERVICES. ONLY THE DEVOTION AND LOYALTY OF ITS SUPPORTING 
CONSTITUENCY, AND OF ITS WORKING FORCES BOTH LAY AND SECRET} 
ARIAL, HAVE ENABLED IT TO SURVIVE THE BATTLE FOR EXISTENCE 
WHICH HAS BEEN FOUGHT THROUGHOUT THE YEARe WHEN WE HEAR THE 
DEPRESSING ROCL=CALL OF YelbeCeA*S THROUGHOUT THE WORLD, WE 
ARE GRATEFUL THAT NONE OF OUR BRANCHES OR DEPARTMENTS HAS 
BEEN CLOSED AND THAT NONE OF OUR SECRETARIAL STAFF HAS BEEN 
DISPENSED WITH EXCEPT FOR PURPOSES OF RETIREMENT OR TRANSFER. 
NOT ONLY HAS THE VOLUME OF SERVICES RENDERED BEEN MUCH THE 
LARGEST IN OUR HISTORY, BUT ALSO IT WOULD BE FAIR TO SAY 
THAT IN POINT OF QUALITY THE YEAR HAS BEEN QUITE A NOTABLE 
ONE 


FOREIGN SERVICE: 


OUR ASSOCIATION HAS CONTINUED TO ASSUME ITS FULL 
SHARE IN THE COST OF MAINTAINING THE CANADIAN SECRETARIES 
ON THE STAFF OF THE INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE WHO ARE AT 
WORK WITH THEIR COLLEAGUES IN SOME THIRTY-ONE COUNTRIES 
OF THE WORLO. THE AMOUNT OF MONEY RAISED BY US FOR THIS 
SERVICE LAST YEAR WAS $16,654.42, WHICH REPRESENTS A 
REDUCTION OVER THE PREVIOUS YEAR OF $2,117.64, OR I1%e 
THE DECREASE IN THE CANADIAN ASSOCIATIONS AS A WHOLE IN 
THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS FOR FOREIGN WORK WAS NEARLY 15%, ANO 
THE DECREASE IN ASSOCIATIONS IN CANADA AND THE UNITED S 
STATES WAS 26%.

DURING THE YEAR, MRe WILBERT SMITH, FORMERLY OF 
CAIRO, MADE TWO VISITS TO MONTREAL AND MADE AN EXTRAORDIN~ 
ARY CONTRIBUTION TO OUR INTERNATIONAL PROGRAM. IT 1S 
DOUBTFUL IF ANY SECRETARY REPRESENTING THE FOREIGN WORK HAS 
EVER MADE A MORE {IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTION TO’ THE UNDERSTAND=- 
ING OF THE INTERNATIONAL SITUATION OR HAS SHOWN MORE CLEARLY 
THE PLACE OF THE YeMeCeAe IN RELATION THERETO»’ THIS PRESENT 
ATION OF THE FOREIGN WORK TO SUCH A LARGE NUMBER OF OUR 
ORGANIZED GROUPS BROUGHT THE INTERNATIONAL BROTHERHOOD IDEA 
TO THE RANK AND FILE OF OUR MEMBERSHIP IN A WAY NEVER 
ACCOMPLISHED SO FULLY GEFOREe 


NATIONAL COUNCIL: 


THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION HAS MAINTAINED ITS TRADITION 
OF CLOSE CO-OPERATION WITH OTHER CANADIAN ASSOCIATIONS THROUGH 
THE NATIONAL COUNCIL OF CANADAe WITH CONDITIONS AS DIFFICULT 
AS WE HAVE KNOWN THEM IN MONTREAL, IT 1S EASY TO UNDERSTAND 
THAT ASSOCIATIONS IN THE SMALLER CITIES AND TOWNS HAVE FOUND 
THEMSELVES FACING AN ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE TASK. BUILDINGS AND 
EQUIPMENT ARE BEING USED TO CAPACITY AND ACTIVITIES HAVE 
NEVER BEEN GREATER, BUT THE STEADY DECLINE IN INCOME HAS 
FORCED FURTHER REDUCTIONS IN STAFF WITH LONGER HOURS OF WORK 
AND REDUCED SALARIES AT ALMOST EVERY POINT ACROSS THE COUNTRY. 
IN A NUMBER OF CITIES THE ACCUMULATED DEFICITS OF PREVIOUS 
YEARS HAVE BEEN PUT INTO LONG TERM LOANSe IN MOST CASES THE 
LOANS ARE RELATIVELY SMALL, BUT THIS ACTION HAS RELIEVED BANK 
CREDITe WITH A FEW EXCEPTIONS, IT 1S BELIEVED THAT BALANCED 
OPERATING BUDGETS HAVE AT LAST BEEN ENSURED. ONE OF THE MOST 
ENCOURAGING FEATURES OF THE PAST THREE YEARS HAS BEEN THE 
STEADINESS OF PUBLIC SUPPORT IN ANNUAL CAMPAIGNS AND THE ~ 
RAPID RISE IN THE NUMBER OF CONTRIBUTORS. THE RETURN OF MORE 
NORMAL ECONOMIC CONDITIONS WILL FIND MANY LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS 
IN A BETTER POSITION THAN EVER TO MOVE FORWARD. 


TWO SMALL RAILROAD ASSOCIATIONS HAVE CLOSED DURING 
THE YEAR, BUT THE NUMBER OF CITY ASSOCIATIONS REMAINS THE 
SAME AS IN #932 AND ONLY ONE LESS THAN IN 4929. THE MEMBERS 
OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL STAFF HAVE PLAYED AN IMPORTANT PART 
IN THE LOCAL SITUATIONS, AND IN SOME CASES HAVE RENDERED 
OUTSTANDING LEADERSHIP. 


THERE HAS BEEN A CONTINUED DECLINE IN THE NUMBER OF 
MEN ON THE SECRETARIAL STAFF, CHIEFLY AMONG THE YOUNGER MEN 
AND THOSE WITH LITTLE TRAINING. NEVERTHELESS THE MOVEMENT 
HAS LOST A NUMBER OF HIGHLY COMPETENT MEN WHO ARE GREATLY 
NEEDED AT THIS TIMEe 


ON THE OTHER HAND, THE ASSOCIATION 1S EMBARRASSED 
BY THE FACT THAT A NUMBER OF MEN WHO HAVE SPENT THE LAST 
FOUR OR FIVE YEARS IN TRAINING ARE NOW GRADUATING FROM 
COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES AND IT 1S IMPOSSIBLE TO PLACE 
THEM IN POSITIONS. THERE 1S A STRONG SENTIMENT AMONG MANY 
BOARDS AND SECRETARIES IN FAVOR OF STAFF TRANSFERS AND 
SOME CHANGES HAVE ALREADY PROVEN ADVANTAGEOUS, 


THE PROGRAM COMMITTEE OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL HAS 
RELEASED A CONSIDERABLE NUMBER OF EXCELLENT PROGRAM OUT- 
LINES WHICH HAVE BEEN OF GREAT VALUE TO LOCAL, ASSOCIATIONS 
WHOSE PROGRAMS OF FORUMS AND STUDY GROUPS HAVE BEEN STEADILY 
INCREASING IN THESE RECENT YEARS. 


IN PLACE OF THE USUAL*ANNUAL MEETING OF THE COUNCIL, 
IN 1933 A SERIES OF REGIONAL CONFERENCES HAVE BEEN HELD AT 
VANCOUVER, CALGARY, WINNIPEG, TORONTO AND SACKVILLE, W!TH 
AN ATTENDANCE OF ABOUT 400. 


ONE OF THE MOST SIGNIFICANT PROJECTS OF THE NATIONAL 
COUNCIL’ IS THE EXTENSION OF THE TRAINING PROGRAM AT LAKE 
COUCHICHING TO INCLUDE REPRESENTATIVES OF OTHER AGENCIES 
HAVING SIMILAR PROBLEMS AND INTERESTS. THE FIRST MEETING 
OF THE INSTITUTE ON POLITICS AND ECONOMICS SECURED A REGIST- 
RATION OF 420 ANDO ESTABLISHED NEW LINES OF COOPERATION 
BETWEEN THE YeMeCeAe AND OTHER NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS. THIS 
INSTITUTE WILL BE REPEATED THIS YEAR AND WILL BE FOLLOWED BY 
A CONFERENCE ON RELIGION AND A SCHOOL FOR LEADERS OF RECREAT- 
1ONe 


THROUGH THE NATIONAL COUNCIL, THE LOCAL ASSOCIATIONS 
ALSO HELPED TO SUPPORT THE WORK OF THE WORLD'S COMMITTEE AT 
GENEVA, AND KEEPS IN CLOSE WORKING RELATIONSHIPS WITH THE 
NATIONAL COUNCILS OF THE UNITED STATES AND GREAT BRITAIN. 


FINANCE ANO PROPERTY: 


DURING THE FISCAL YEAR JUST CLOSED $14,800.49 WAS 
PAID ON ACCOUNT OF PLEDGES AND UNDERWRITINGS TO OUR BUILOING 
FUND, LEAVING A BALANCE OF $171,503.21 STILL TO BE COLLECTED 
IN ORDER THAT WE MAY BE ABLE TO REASONABLY REOUCE OUR EXCESS 
MORTGAGE LOAN AND LATER ON ERECT THE NOTRE DAME DE’ GRACE 
BUILDING, AND THUS COMPLETE OUR BUILDING PROGRAM, THE SUM 
OF $10,000.00 WAS PAID IN REDUCTION OF THE MORTGAGE LOAN, 
WHICH NOW STANDS AT $390.000e00- THE ASSOCIATION HAS THE 
PRIVILEGE OF PAYING A MAXIMUM OF $50,000.00 IN ANY YEAR THAT 
RECEIPTS FROM LEGACIES OR OTHER SOURCES MAKE !T POSSIBLE. 
WHEN ONE REALIZES THAT THE OPERATING DEFICIT FOR THE YEAR 
EQUALLED THE AMOUNT OF INTEREST AND EXCHANGE PAID ON OUR 
MORTGAGE LOAN, IT WILL BE SEEN THAT FURTHER PAYMENTS ON 
ACCOUNT OF OUR BUILDING FUNO PLEDGES WOULD BE OF THE GREATEST 
ASSISTANCE IN OUR OPERATING FINANCES. 


IN. THE, FIRST MONTH OF OUR FISCAL YEAR, THE ANNUAL 
MAINTENANCE CANVASS WAS CONDUCTED UNDER THE GENERAL CHAIR- 
MANSHIP OF MRe JOHN Be. FROSST, WHEN 2,678 SUBSCRIPTIONS WERE 
SECURED TOTALLING $70,380.00. THIS WAS LATER INCREASED TO 
$74,007245, OF WHICH $72,087295 WAS ACTUALLY PAID IN CASH 
PRIOR TO THE CLOSING OF OUR BOOKS. THE ABOVE RESULT REPRE- 
SENTS A DECREASE IN SUBSCRIPTIONS OVER THE PREVIOUS YEAR OF 
$13,410.23, OR 15%, AND IN THE LAST TWO YEARS OF $30,248.00 
OR 30%. THERE WAS A DECREASE OF 75 CIVIC MEMBERSHIPS FROM 
LAST YEAR, OR 141 IN THE LAST TWO YEARS. IT 1S GRATIFYING 
TO OBSERVE, HOWEVER, THAT THE CAMPAIGN EXPENSES WERE REDUCED 
FROM $5,765.00 TO $2,766.00. NEARLY 600 CANVASSERS WERE 
ENROLLED FOR THE \EFFORT, AND AN AVERAGE OF 200 ATTENDED THE 
DAILY REPORT LUNCHEONS WHICH WERE ALL HELD IN THE ASSOCIAT= 
10ON BUILDING. 


THE DECREASE IN THE ASSOCIATION'S INCOME MADE IT 
NECESSARY TO MAKE A SECOND REDUCTION IN SALARIES AND WAGES 
ON JANUARY IST. AGGREGATING ABOUT $12,000600 PER ANNUM. 
STAFF RETIREMENTS, TRANSF RS AND RESIGNATIONS ALSO RESULTED 
IN IMPORTANT REDUCTIONS }IN PAYROLL EXPENSE. 


THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENT OF THE METRO- 
POLITAN BOARD, EXCLUSIVE OF THE REGISTRATION BUREAU AND 
CAMPS, INDICATES A TOTAL INCOME OF $368,149.79, AND AN 
EXPENDITURE OF $394,446.03, LEAVING A DEFICIT OF $26,296.24. 
WHEN ONE CONSIDERS, HOWEVER, THAT THE NOTRE DAME DE GRACE 
BUDGET WAS FOR THE FIRST TIME INCLUDED IN OUR OPERATING 
ACCOUNTS; THAT THE PAVING TAXES INCREASED $1,500.00; THAT 
THE METROPOLITAN PROGRAM STAFF WAS AUGMENTED; THAT THE 
INTEREST PAID BY THE ASSOCIATION INCREASED $17,046672; THAT 
SUBSCRIPTIONS FELL OFF $13,410.23, MEMBERSHIP $6,782.26, 


-COLLEGE $1,200.00, WHILE AT THE SAME TIME THE PROGRAM OF THE 


ASSOCIATION WAS \MMENSELY INCREASED, THERE !S MUCH FOR WHICH 
TO BE GRATEFUL. BUT, AN ACCRUED DEFICIT OF OVER $50,000.00 
1S A SERIOUS MATTER, AND HELP FROM FRIENDS WHO HAVE NOT YET 
SUBSCRIBED TO OUR CURRENT FUNDS, OR WHO ARE IN ARREARS WITH 
PAYMENTS OF THEIR SUBSCRIPTIONS, WILL BE-VITALLY HELPFUL. 


IT IS OF PASSING INTEREST THAT THE ASSOCIATION HAS 
MAINTAINED ITS FULL CONTRIBUTION OF $9,000.00 TO THE IMPORT- 
ANT WORK OF THE NATIONAL COUNCIL; THAT YOUR METROPOLITAN 
BOARD RECENTLY REFUSED AN OFFER OF $50,000.00 FOR THE 
PURCHASE OF THE NORTH BRANCH BUILDING WHICH IS CARRIED ON 
OUR BOOKS AT $99,865.00; AND THAT THE FIRE LOSS IN THE MOUNT 
ROYAL AVENUE BRANCH AMOUNTING TO $350.00 WAS FULLY COVERED 
BY INSURANCE.

METROPOLITAN RESIDENCE BUILDING: 


THE YEAR JUST CLOSED HAS AGAIN PROVEN THE WISDOM OF 
OPERATING THE DRUMMOND=STANLEY STREET BUILDING AS A UNIT 
SEPARATE FROM THE CENTRAL BRANCH, THE COLLEGE AND THE METRO- 
POLITAN BOARO. THERE HAS BEEN ANOTHER STRIKING ADVANCE IN 
BOTH QUALITY AND QUANTITY IN THE PROGRAM FOR THE RESIDENCE, 
THE MEMBERS, AND THE COMMUNITY GROUPS USING THE BUILDING. 

IN VIEW OF THE CLOSE RELATIONSHIP OF THE BUILDING TO THE 
FINANCING OF OUR WORK THROUGHOUT THE CITY, SOME DETAILED 
FIGURES FOR THE YEAR WILL BE OF PARTICULAR INTEREST. 


OF THE 600 ROOMS IN THE BUILDING, THERE HAS BEEN AN 
AVERAGE OCCUPANCY OF 420 THROUGHOUT THE YEAR, OR 70%, THE 
HIGHEST FIGURE BEING 568 ON MARCH 18TH AND THE LOWEST BEING 
364 ON JUNE 24THe IN ALL, 5,985 DIFFERENT MEN, WITH AN 
AVERAGE AGE OF 32 YEARS, WERE IN RESIDENCE DURING THE PERIOD 
UNDER REVIEW; 625 WHO WERE OUT OF WORK OR WHO WERE IN NEED 
OF ASSISTANCE HAVE BEEN GIVEN FREE ACCOMMODATION OR AT 
SPECIAL RATESe SPECIAL RATES WERE ALSO EXTENDED TO STUDENTS, 
AND 75 MCGILL UNIVERSITY UNDERGRADUATES WERE IN THE BUILDING 
DURING THE COLLEGE SEASON. THE GROSS EARNINGS OF THE RESID- 
ENCE BUILDING WERE $92,015.71, AND INCREASE OF $10,064.46 
OVER THE PREVIOUS YEAR, OR NEARLY $1,000.00 PER MONTH. 


THE LATEST FIGURE FOR THE YeMeCeA'S ON THIS CONTINENT 
INDICATES THAT THE PERCENTAGE OF DORMITORY OCCUPANCY IN 
1932 WAS 63%. - 

IT WiLL BE RECALLED THAT THE TWO TOP FLOORS OF THE 
DRUMMOND=STANLEY STREET BUILDING WERE NOT FURNISHED WHEN 
THE BUILDING WAS OPENED TWO YEARS AGO» DUE TO THE DEMAND 
LAST SEPTEMBER, IT WAS DECIDED To COMPLETE THE FURNISHING 
OF THE ENTIRE BUILDING. IN CONNECTION WITH THIS WORK, GIFTS 
IN KIND WERE RECEIVED FROM -THE CANADIAN FAIRBANKS MORSE 
COMPANY, SIMMONS BED COMPANY, WOODS MANUFACTURING COMPANY, 
CANADIAN JOHNS=MANVILLE COMPANY, AND THE ‘NATIONAL CASH REG- 
ISTER COMPANY. ' ' ‘ 


AT THE CONCLUSION OF THE YEAR'S GUARANTEE OF THE 
FOUNDATION COMPANY, IMPORTANT REPAIRS WERE MADE TO THE 
BUILDING, AND IN ADDITION A CONSIDERABLE AMOUNT OF RETINT= 
ING AND DECORATING WAS DONE BY OUR OWN STAFF. THE MAIN 
ITEMS WERE THE SOLARIUM, BARBER SHOP, LOCKER ‘ROOMS, SWIMM= 
ING POOL CEILING, LUNCH COUNTER, RESIDENCE ROOMS, BOILERS 
AND ASH HOIST REBUILT, HOT WATER HEATERS CLEANED AND 
PAINTED INSIDE, VACUUM PUMPS CLEANED AND REPACKEDe. 


DURING OCTOBER, ARRANGEMENTS WERE COMPLETED WHEREBY 
DRe WMe MOFFATT OF THE ROYAL VICTORIA HOSPITAL STAFF WAS 
GIVEN AN OFFICE IN THE BUILDING AND IS AVAILABLE TO THE 
RESIDENTS. THIS HAS PROVEN TO BE A DEFINITELY FORWARD STEP. 


FOR TWENTY YEARS THE ASSOCIATION HAS OPERATED A 
LAUNDRY SERVICE IN THE DRUMMOND STREET BUILDING IN ORDER 
TO TAKE CARE OF THE “FLATWORK OF THE CENTRAL BRANCHe ON 
OCTOBER 47TH, HOWEVER, THE INSTALLATION OF EQUIPMENT FOR 
DOING PERSONAL LAUNORY WAS COMPLETED, AND SINCE THAT TIME 
AN AVERAGE OF 168 YOUNG MEN WEEKLY HAVE MADE USE OF THE 
FACILITIES. OVER 400 ‘DIFFERENT YOUNG MEN HAVE USED THE 
FACILITIES EACH MONTH. AT THE PRESENT TIME THE LAUNORY 
1S DOING ALL OF THE WORK OF THE RESIDENCE BUILDING, THE 
CENTRAL AND WESTMOUNT BRANCHES, CAMPS OTOREKE AND KANAWANA, 
AS WELL AS THE MAJOR PORTION OF THE RESIDENTS' PERSONAL 
WORKe THE MONTHLY AVERAGE WAS 45,860 PIECES, WHICH IT IS 
STATED REPRESENTS MORE WORK THAN THAT BEING DONE BY THE 
WINDSOR AND QUEEN'S HOTELS COMBINED. 


MEMBERSHIP: 


THE PAID MEMBERSHIP OF THE ASSOCIATION ON MARCH 
31ST WAS 6,004 COMPARED WITH 6,472 A YEAR AGO, A DECREASE 
OF 468. THERE WERE, HOWEVER, FREE MEMBERSHIPS ISSUED TO 
1,569 UNEMPLOYED THIS YEAR COMPARED WITH 1,181 LAST YEAR, 
AND IF THIS LATTER GROUP 1S COUNTED AS MEMBERS, THERE IS 
AN §NCREASE IN THE YEAR OF 106 


THESE FIGURES, OF COURSE, DO NOT INCLUDE THE 
HUNDREDS OF YOUNG MEN AND BOYS, AND IN SOME BRANCHES WOMEN 
AND GIRLS, WHO BECOME MEMBERS OF THE ASSOCIATION ONLY FOR 
THE SUMMER MONTHS OR TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF OUR SHORT-TERM 
MEMBERSHIP, NOR DO THEY INCLUDE THE THOUSANDS OF YOUNG 
PEOPLE WHO USE OUR DIFFERENT BUILDINGS AS COMMUNITY CENTRES, 
NOR THE CONSTANT STREAM OF NEWCOMERS TO OUR CITY ANO OTHERS 
WHO ARE SERVED BY OUR ASSOCIATION WITHOUT REGARD TO THE 
FACT OF THEIR MEMBERSHIP.

AMOUNT SUBJECT TO 10% DISCOUNT WHEN PAID IN ADVANCE.

AMONG THE UNIQUE FEATURES OF THE YEAR WAS THE OBSERV- 
ANCE OF FOUNDERS' WEEK IN OCTOBER, WHEN ELEVEN MEETINGS WERE 
HELD IN THE DIFFERENT BRANCHES WITH A TOTAL ATTENDANCE OF 745.6 
IN ADDITION TO HONORING THE MEMORY OF THE FOUNDER, SIR GEORGE 
WILLIAMS, ALL OF THE BRANCHES TOOK OCCASION TO SECURE THE 
ATTENDANCE OF AS MANY OF THE FOUNDERS OF THEIR RESPECTIVE 
BRANCHES AS POSSIBLE, AND THE MEETINGS WERE VOTED BY ALL WHO 
ATTENDED AS OF VERY GREAT SIGNIFICANCE. IT WAS THE OPINION 
OF THE COMMITTEE IN CHARGE OF FOUNDERS* WEEK THAT THIS SHOULD 
BE MADE.AN ANNUAL EVENT. 


UNEW PLOYMENT: 


THE WORK BEGUN BY THE ASSOCIATION SO VIGOROUSLY EIGHT- 
EEN MONTHS AGO IN THE INTERESTS OF THE UNEMPLOYED HAS BEEN 
GREATLY INTENSIFIED DURING THE YEAR BECAUSE OF CONDITIONS WHICH 
HAVE ALREADY BEEN REFERRED TO IN THIS REPORT. THE MAJOR SER= 
VICE HAS BEEN CARRIED ON. IN-THESUN LIFE BUILDING BY THE REGIST= 
RATION BUREAU FOR OFFICE WORKERS. THE BUREAU HAS BEEN OPERATED 
BY THE YeleCeAe IN GLOSE CO-OPERATION WITH THE MONTREAL COUNCIL 
OF SOCIAL AGENCIES, THE EMERGENCY UNEMPLOYMENT RELIEF COMMITTEE, 
ANO THE MONTREAL RELIEF COMMITTEE. THIS WORK REPRESENTS A DEF- 
INITE AND WELL=PLANNED EFFORT TO MEET AND, IN SO FAR AS .POSSIBLE, 
COUNSEL, ASSIST ANO RELIEVE THOSE IN DISTRESS CAUSED BY THE 
ECONOMIC CONDITIONS THROUGH WHICH WE ARE PASSING. r 

STATISTICS CONVEY A VERY INADEQUATE PICTURE OF THE 
SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS SERVICE, YET THE RECORDS INDICATE THAT 
DURING THE PAST YEAR 3,017 MEN REGISTERED FOR EMPLOYMENT, OF 
WHICH NUMBER 310 WERE PLACED IN PERMANENT OR TEMPORARY POSI- 
TIONS. IN ADDITION TO GIVING ADVICE CONCERNING ‘EMPLOYMENT 
AND CO-OPERATING IN THE SECURING OF POSITIONS, THE BUREAU 
HAS BEEN ONE OF THE RECOGNIZEO AGENCIES IN THE DISTRIBUTION 
OF RELIEF FOR BOTH FAMILIES AND SHNGLE MEN IN THE SO=CALLED 
WHITE COLLAR GROUP, AND AT THE PRESENT Fis HAS 375 FAMILIES 
AND 835 SINGLE MEN ON ITS L18T. : 


THE CONTRIBUTION TO THE PHYSICAL NEEDS OF THESE MEN 
HAS BEEN, OF COURSE, OF THE GREATEST “IMPORTANCE, BUT THE 
BUREAU HAS RENDERED VALUABLE SERVICE IN ASSISTING WITH VOC- 
ATIONAL TESTS AND COUNSEL; CO-OPERATION WITH THE SIR GEORGE 
WILLIAMS COLLEGE; IN REGISTERING 200 MEN FOR THE SPEENDID 
SERIES OF AFTERNOON LECTURES GIVEN LAST WINTER IN STRATHCONA 
HALL BY THE EXTRA=MURAL, DEPARTMENT OF MCGILL UNIVERSITY;, AND 
BY ARRANGING SOCIALS, CONCERTS, AND VaeTUReR IN THE ¥oMeCeAc 
BUILDINGS,

CiTY-WIDE BOYS' WORK: 


WHILE THERE HAS BEEN A DECIDED FALLING-OFF IN THE 
NUMBER OF BOYS WHO ARE PAYING MEMBERS OF THE ASSOCIATION, 
OUR BRANCHES HAVE CARRIED A HEAVIER LOAD OF ACTIVITIES THAN 
EVER BEFORE. THERE HAS BEEN A COINCIDENT INCREASE IN THE 
EFFECTIVE USE OF VOLUNTEER LEADERSHIP, AND A GROWING EMPHASIS 
ON THE QUALITATIVE ASPECTS OF OUR PROGRAM. REFERENCE HAS BEEN 
MADE ELSEHWERE IN THIS REPORT TO THE SERVICE FOR UUNEMPLOYED 
BOYS WHO HAVE USED OUR BUILDINGS IN EVEN LARGER NUMBERS THAN 
EVER BEFORE. ; 


AMONG THE INTER=BRANCH COMPETITIVE EVENTS HAVE BEEN 
BASEBALL, BASKETBALL, SWIMMING AND PING=PONG, 


DUE TO PRESENT ECONOMIC CONDITIONS, THERE HAS BEEN A 
DEFINITE CHANGE IN THE BOYS' GROUP WITH WHOM THE ASSOCIATION 
DOES ITS MOST WORKe WITH THEEEXCEPTION OF THE WESTMOUNT 
BRANCH, FOR MANY YEARS THE MAIN CONSTITUENCY OF THE ASSOCIAT~ 
1ON HAS BEEN WITH EMPLOYED BOYS. THE BUSINESS DEPRESSION HAS 
COMPLETELY CHANGED THIS, AND OUR EMPLOYED BOYS GROUPS IS VERY 
APPRECIABLY SMALLER THAN EVER BEFORE. ON THE OTHER HAND, THERE 
HAS BEEN A VERY IMPORTANT GROWTH IN OUR SERVICE TO SCHOOL 
BOYS. IN THE CENTRAL BRANCH THE IMPACT HAS BEEN SUCH AS TO 
CALL FORTH THE HIGHEST PRAISE FROM SCHOOL MASTERS. IN THE 
NORTH BRANCH, A VACATION SCHOOL ENROLLED 125 BOYS WITH AN 
AVERAGE ATTENDANCE OF 112~- THESE BOYS MET FIVE MORNINGS A 
WEEK THROUGHOUT THE SUMMER, COURSES BEING GIVEN IN MUSIC, 
BASKETRY, ART APPRECIATION, CITIZENSHIP AND SWIMMING. 


THE 'H1t-Y* MOVEMENT WHICH UNITES THOSE BOYS INTER- 
ESTED IN CREATING, MAINTAINING AND EXTENOING HIGH STANDARDS 
OF CHRISTIAN CHARACTER THROUGHOUT THE SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY, 
HAS BEEN MORE USEFUL THAN EVERe THE WESTMOUNT BRANCH HAS 
HAO THE LARGEST CLUB IN ITS HISTORY; NOTRE DAME DE GRACE 
HAS HAD A VERY EFFECTIVE GROUP FROM WIESTHILL, AND A NEW CLUB 
HAS BEEN ORGANIZED IN THE CENTRAL BRANCH, ENROLLING BOYS 
FROM NONTREAL HIGH AND LACHINEe AT A RALLY OF tHi-¥* CLUBS,

AN OUTSTANDING INCIDENT IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE 
COLLEGE HAS BEEN THE INAUGURATION OF A DAY PROGRAM, DURING 
THE PAST YEAR, IN THE JUNIOR COLLEGE OF ARTS, SCIENCE AND 
COMMERCE. THIS NEW PROGRAM, WHICH HAS COMPLETED ITS FIRST 
YEAR SUCCESSFULLY, ENABLES PARENTS OF GREATER MONTREAL TO 
PLACE THEIR SONS AND DAUGHTERS WHO HAVE GRADUATED FROM HIGH 
SCHOOL IN A TWO-YEAR COLLEGE COURSE UNDER ASSOCIATION AUSPICES 
WITH CLOSE SUPERVISION FROM INSTRUCTORS AND COUNSELLORS. IT 
{1S FELT BY SOME OF US THAT SUCH A PROGRAM HAS BEEN A NEED IN 
THIS CITY AND THAT IT WILL BE THE MEANS OF ASSISTING LARGE 
NUMBERS OF OLDER BOYS ANDO GIRLS TO MAV'E A BETTER ADJUSTMENT 
TO THEIR LATER PROFESSIONAL TRAINING IN THE UPPER YEARS OF 
THE UNIVERSITY; OR, IF THEY DO NOT PROCEED BEYOND THE JUNIOR 
COLLEGE, TO THE VARIOUS OCCUPATIONS WHICH THEY WILL ENTER 
EVENTUALLY. 


WE ARE GRATIFIED BY THE RESPONSE WHICH HAS BEEN MADE 
TO THIS NEW DEVELOPMENT, ANDO COMMEND THE JUNIOR COLLEGE TO 
THE CONSIDERATION OF THE MEMBERS OF OUR BOARDS OF MANAGEMENT 
AS A POSSIBILITY FOR THEIR OWN OLDER BOYS AND GIRLS.

RELIGIOUS WORK: 


THE ASSOCIATION WAS FOUNDED AND HAS BEEN BUILT UPON 
THE PRINCEPLE THAT ALL OF LIFE HAS RELIGIOUS IMPLICATIONS. 
THE POLICY..OF THOUGHFULLY ENDEAVORING, TO PLACE A CHRISTIAN 
EMPHASIS ,ON ALL OF ITS PROGRAM HAS, CONTINUED AND IT 1S ENCOUR@ 
AGING TO OBSERVE THE EVER WIDENING ACCEPTANCE OF THIS PHIL= 
OSOPHY IN CONNECTION WITH ITS WORKe THERE HAS, OF COURSE 
BEEN A GREAT VOLUME OF SPECIFICALLY RELIGIOUS WORK CARRIED 
ON WITH A WIDE VARIETY OF METHODS. THESE, |NCLUDED PERSONAL 
INTERVIEWS, DISCUSSION AND STUDY GROUPS, CONFERENCES AND 
FORUMS, FIRESIDE SING-SONGS, SUNDAY AFTERNOON MUSICALES, AND 
TEAS FOR YOUNG MEN LIVING AWAY FROM HOME, CAMPFLRE TALKS AND 
DEVOTIONS, RESIDENTS! MEMBERS SUNDAY MORNING BREAKFASTS, 
OXFORD GROUP IN CENTRAL BRANCH, FOREIGN SERVICE MEETINGS 
AND BIBLE CLASSES.

CITY WIDE RELATIONSHIPS: 


IT HAS BEEN THE POLICY OF THE YeMeCeAse FOR YEARS TO 
ALLY ITSELF WITH MANY ORGANIZATIONS WORKING FOR’ BETTER SOCIAL, 
EDUCATIONAL AND RELIGIOUS CONDITIONSe AS A RESULT, MUCH HAS 
BEEN IMPOSSIBLE OF ACHIEVEMENT. THESE EXTRA SERVICES OF THE 
ASSOCIATION MAKE IT ONE OF THE’ INDISPENSABLE SERVICE INSTITU- 
TIONS IN THE COMMUNITY. IN SOME CASES THE PART WHICH THE 
YelieCeAe HAS PLAYED HAS’ BEEN A RELATIVELY SMALL ONE, SUCH AS 
GRANTING THE USE OF A ROOM IN ONE OF OUR BUILDINGS AS A PLACE 
OF MEETING. AT OTHER TIMES IT HAS MADE A CONTRIBUTION OF 
FIRST IMPORTANCE, SUCH AS THAT OF A MEMBER OF OUR STAFF BEING 
CHAIRMAN OF THE EDUCATION AND RECREATION DIVISION OF THE 
MONTREAL COUNCIL OF SOCIAL: AGENCIES, OR SUPERINTENDENT OF ONE 
OF THE LARGEST SUNDAY SCHOOLS. ON THE ISLAND OF MONTREAL.

KAMP KANAWANA: 


THE ‘SEASON OF 1932 WAS THE 23RD IN WHICH OUR BoYs' r 
CAMP HAS BEEN OPERATED IN ITS PRESENT LOCATION. THE ATTEND= 
ANCE WAS THE THIRD LARGEST IN OUR HISTORY. THE BOYS WERE 
REGISTERED AS FOLLOWS: 


CENTRAL cocccececcere 130 
WESTMOUNT ecccceccceee 127 
NOTRE DAME DE GRACE+e 37 
NORTH BRANCHeececesses 34 
SOUTHWESTERNesccceces 23 
MOUNT ROYAL cccececces 8 


360 


THERE WERE NO BOYS PRESENT FROM. INTERNATIONAL BRANCH 
OR POINT STe CHARLES. THE AVERAGE LENGTH OF STAY WAS 3.23 
WEEKS. 


THE STAFF AND LEADERS OF THE CAMP REFLECTED THE PLANS 
WHICH WERE MADE IN ADVANCE, INCLUDING THE TRAINING COURSE FOR 
LEADERS HELD IN THE CENTRAL BRANCH IN THE LATE WINTER AND 
SPRING MONTHSe .THE.PROGRAM WAS EVEN MORE EXTENSIVE THAN IN 
PREVIOUS YEARS AND WAS FINELY EDUCATIONAL IN ITS CONTENT. CON 
SIDERABLE IMPROVEMENT WAS MADE IN THE CAMP RECORDS, AND THERE 
WAS AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF PARENTS AND FRIENDS PAYING 
A VISIT TO THE CAMP. WE ARE INDEBTED TO MR. DENT HARRISON FOR 
SPENDING TWO DAYS IN CAMP MAKING A FIVE HUNDRED FOOT MOTION 
FILM PICTURE FIOM WHICH HAS SUBSEQUENTLY BEEN USED IN THE 
PROMOTION OF THE CAMP IN THE DIFFERENT BRANCHES ANDO IN SEVERAL 
HOMES. 


PROBABLY THE MOST SERIOUS PROBLEM THE CAMP IS FACING 
AT THE PRESENT TIME 1S THAT OF AN ADEQUATE WATER SUPPLY. THE 
FACT THAT BOTH WELLS PRESENTLY BEING USED WERE DRY DURING THE 
PAST SEASON LEADS ONE TO BELIEVE THAT IT IS SURFACE WATER WHICH 
1S BEING USED. AT LEAST ONE MORE WELL WILL HAVE TO BE PROVIDED 
FOR IN THE NEAR FUTURE. 


CAMP _OTOREKE: 


THE 1932 SEASON AT CAMP OTOREKE MARKED THE 41ST YEAR 
OF OUR ACTIVITY ON LAC ST.JOSEPH AND THIS CAMP SITE REMAINS ONE 
OF THE MOST BEAUTIFUL IN THE PROVINCE.) SIXTY=SEVEN CAMPERS 
FROM SIX OF OUR BRANCHES AND THREE FROM NEW YORK CITY WERE IN 
ATTENDANCE, A TOTAL OF SEVENTY, WHICH !S SLIGHTLY LESS THAN 
DURING THE PREVIOUS YEARe IN ADDITION, THIRTY-SEYEN PERSONS 
VISITED OTOREKE FOR WEEK=ENDS, MAKING ONE HUNDREO AND SEVEN 
DIFFERENT PERSONS IN ALLe THIS COMPARES WITH ONE HUNDRED ONE 
YEAR AGOe 


IT 1S ALSO GRATIFYING TO KNOW THAT THE CAMP OPERATED 
WITH A SURPLUS OF $177200 TO APPLY AGAINST THE DEFICITS OF FOR- 
MER YEARS AMOUNTING TO $916.00, WHICH IS CARRIED IN SUSPENSE. 
THIS RESULT IS PARTICULARLY GRATIFYING IN VIEW OF THE FACT 
THAT IT WAS FELT THAT WE COULD NOT OPERATE THE CAMP LAST YEAR 
UNDER THE GENERAL CONDITIONS PREVIALING. 


COMMITTEE SERVICE: . 


THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION HAS ALWAYS RECOGNIZED THE 
VALUES WHICH INHERE IN THE COMMITTEE SERVICE OF THE ASSOC- 
1ATEON ANDO ITS LAYMEN HAVE CONSEGUENTLY OCCUPIED A COMMANDING 
PLACE IN THE MOVEMENT IN CANADA AND THROUGHOUT THE WORLD. 
THESE VALUES ACCRUE BOTH TO THE ASSOCIATION ANO TO THE INDIV- 
IMDUAL RENDERING THE SERVICE. THE VALUES TO THE ASSOCIATION 


ARE OBVIOUS AND MANY LEADERS OF OUR MOVEMENT THROUGHOUT THE 
WORLD TESTIFY TO THE ‘BENEFITS THAT HAVE COME INTO THEIR OWN 
LIVES THROUGH THIS "SERVICEs THE DEVELOPMENT OF QUALITIES OF 
PERSONALITY AND CHARACTER, AS WELL AS ABILITIES AND SKILL, 
THROUGH MUTUAL CO-OPERATION IN UNDERSTANDING AND WORTHWHILE 
ACTIVITIES, 1S A PRINCIPLE THAT PRESENT DAY EDUCATION RECOG- 
NIZES AS ESSENTIALLY BASIC AND VALID. 


MR. PAUL SUPER SAYS, “ONE OF THE TRUE ACCOMPLISHMENTS 
OF THE YeMeCeA. 1S THE MODERN RE=DISCOVERY OF THE LAYMAN, 
ESPECIALLY THE YOUNG LAYMAN == THE ASSERTION OF HIS PLACE IN 
SPIRITUAL ENTERPRISES AND THE EFFECTIVE DEMONSTRATION OF HIS 
SPHERE AND TALENTS." THE LATE DRe FRANK Ke SANDERS, FOR MANY 
YEARS AN OUTSTANDING LAYMAN OF THE ASSOCIATION, HAS SAID, 
"THE NEED OF EACH INDIVIDUAL #8 TO BE DRAWN INTO AN UNSELFISH 
FELLOWSHIP THAT WILL GIVE HIM AN OBJECTIVE OUTSIDE HIS MERE 
PERSONAL INTERESTS, AN OBJECTIVE WHICH WILL HAVE MUCH TO DO 
WITH THE BROADENING AND DEVELOPING OF HIS RELIGIOUS LIFE." 
IN DRe DOGGETT'S AUTHORITATIVE HISTORY OF THE YeMeCeA. HE 
STATES THAT THE NEW FACTOR WHICH THE YeMeCeAs INTRODUCED INTO 
THE RELIGIOUS LIFE OF 'THE WORLD WAS THE COMMITTEE SYSTEM, AND 
IN A BOOK WHICH MRe JeAe URICE 1S NOW WRITING HE STATES THAT 
THE PRESENT DAY GENIUS OF THE YeMeCeAe LIES IN ITS COMMITTEE 
SERVICE. : : 


NEVER BEFORE IN OUR HISTORY HAVE WE HAD SO LARGE A 
VOLUME OF VOLUNTEER SERVICE ON THE PART OF INTERESTED FRIENOS 
FROM WITHIN AND WITHOUT OUR MEMBERSHIP. IN EVERY BRANCH, AND 
IN PROJECTS OF THE METROPOLITAN BOARD, THERE HAS BEEN AN 
UNPRECEDENTED VOLUME OF UNSELFISH WORK DONE BY VOLUNTEERS. 
A LONG LIST OF EXAMPLES COULD BE GIVEN, EXTENDING FROM THE 
LEADERSHIP OF MR. GORDON TAYLOR, THE YOUNG AMATEUR GOLF CHAMP} 
1ON OF CANADA, TO THE BOYS FROM THE SCHOOL FOR THE BLIND, TO 
THE SPLENDID SERVICE OF THE NEARLY SEVEN HUNDRED WORKERS IN 
THE RECENT FINANCIAL CAMPAIGNe 


ANOTHER OUTSTANDING BIT OF SERVICE WAS THE VISIT OF OUR 
PRESIDENT AS CHAIRMAN. OF. THE NATIONAL COUNCIL TO ELEVEN OF THE 
ASSOCIATIONS IN ONTARIO’ 


ONE OF THE INTERESTING FEATURES OF THE YEAR HAS BEEN 
THE NEW EMPHASIS ON INFORMAL AND UNHURRIED MEETINGS OF GROUPS, 
COMMITTEES AND BOARDS IN WHAT THE OXFORD GROUP CALLS ‘HOUSE 
PARTIES'. THERE IS. NOTHING NEW ABOUT THIS' IDEA IN THE Y.Me 
CeAe, BUT IN NO YEAR HAS IT BEEN DEVELOPED TO THE POINT OF 
THE LAST YEARe FOR EXAMPLE, ONE OF THE MEMBERS OF THE Boys? 
WORK COMMITTEE OF THE CENTRAL BRANCH ENTERTAINED THIS GROUP 
FOR TWO DAYS AT HIS SUMMER HOME AT KNOWLTON WHERE A SPLENDID 
COMBINATION OF FELLOWSHIP AND WORK RESULTED. THE GENERAL 
CHAIRMAN OF OUR RECENT FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN INVITED THE Divis- 
1ON MANAGERS TO LAC BRULE FOR THE SAME PERIOD OF TIME TO 
CONFER ABOUT THE PROJECT WHICH THEY HAD IN HANDe SIGNIFICANT 
HOUSE MEETINGS HAVE ALSO BEEN HELD BY THE CENTRAL BRANCH 
BOARD IN THE HOMES OF THREE OF THEIR MEMBERS. THE VALUES IN 
FELLOWSHIP AND UNDERSTANDING OF OUR WORK THROUGH THESE UN- 
HURRIED GATHERINGS ARE QUITE REMARKABLE. ONE OF THE REASONS, 
IN OUR OPINION, FOR THE VITALITY OF THE NOTRE DAME DE GRACE 
BRANCH LIES IN THE FACT THAT SINCE ITS ORGANIZATION THE 
MEETINGS OF THEIR BOARDS AND COMMITTEES HAVE FREQUENTLY BEEN 
HELD IN THE HOMES OF THE MEMBERSe 


THE RELATION OF LAY SERVICE OF A FINE QUALITY TO THE 
EFFICIENCY OF THE PERMANENT STAFF OF THE ASSOCIATION IS OF 


THE UTMOST IMPORTANCE. THERE, 1S NO SINGLE FACTOR IN DEVEL= 
OPING A STRONG SECRETARIAT MORE. EFFECTIVE THAN THE SYMPATH= 
ETIC AND LOYAL BACKING OF GROUPS OF LAYMEN. CONVERSELY, 
THE LARGEST USE OF LAYMEN IN THE ASSOCIATION'S PROJECTS IS 
INTIMATELY RELATED TO THE TACT AND SKILL OF THE STAFF AT 
THIS POINT. 


WHILE OUR STATISTICAL RECORD FOR THE YEAR 1S NOT 
COMPLETE, SOME WDEA OF THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THE YEAR IN THIS 
RESPECT WILL BE SEEN IN. THE FACT THAT IN THE MONTH OF 
NOVEMBER THERE WERE 96 BOARD OR COMMITTEE MEETINGS WITH AN 
ATTENDANCE OF 888, AND A PERSON=HOURS PARTICIPATION TOTALL- 
ING 1,106. THE FIGURES FOR THE YEAR WOULD BE EXTREMELY 
IMPRESSIVE.

CENTRAL: 


CENTRAL BRANCH, BECAUSE OF ITS LOCATION, IS THE 
MONTREAL ASSOCIATION ON THE JOB, WELCOMING AND SERVING 
NEWCOMERS TO THE CITY. NATURALLY, DUE TO THE GENERAL SIT- 
UATION, NO IMMIGRANTS HAVE BEEN ARRIVING, BUT HUNDREDS 
OF YOUNG MEN HOPING TO IMPROVE THEIR SITUATIONS, HAVE MAN- 
AGED TO GET TO THE CITY, AND USUALLY HAVE ARRIVED PENNI- 
LESS. THESE HAVE BEEN REFERRED TO THE PROPER AGENCIES FOR 
ASSISTANCE, WHILE VARIOUS SERVICES HAVE BEEN RENDERED IN 
OUR OWN BUILDING. 


THE YOUNG MEN'S CABINET AND THE SENIOR DIVISION 
COMMITTEE HAVE BEEN RESPONSIBLE FOR WHAT WE -FEEL HAS BEEN 
IN MANY WAYS THE MOST MEANINGFUL PROGRAM IN YEARS. THE 
SPOKE, Y'S MEN'S, CURRENT EVENTS, CREST, PUBLIC SPEAKING, 
WANT@=TO-SEE-IT, AND GLEE CLUBS, ENLISTED MANY MEMBERS, 
THE INTER-Y DISCUSSION GROUP, THE FELLOWSHIP BIBLE CLASS, 
THE YOUNG MEN'S BIBLE CLASS, SUNDAY MORNING BREAKFAST, 
SONG SERVICE, AFTER CHURCH SUNDAY EVENINGS, SPECIAL EAST- 
ER WEEK SERIES, AND THE OXFORD GROUP, WERE ALL FEATURES OF 
SIGNIFICANCE IN THE LIVES OF THOSE WHO PARTICIPATED. A 
FORUM SERIES, "RECONSTRUCTING CANADIAN LIFE;" A LECTURE 
SERIES, "MAKING RHE MOST OF LIFE," AND VARIOUS ADDRESSES 
ON WORLO BROTHERHOOD, WERE HELPFUL IN WIDENING THE HORI- 
ZONS OF MANYe 


THE PHYSICAL DEPARTMENT CONTINUED TO INTEREST HUN- 
DREDS IN A GREAT VARIETY OF RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES. 
BOXING AND WRESTLING UNDER EXPERT COACHES, BASKETBALL 
HOUSE LEAGUES AND REPRESENTATIVE TEAMS, VOLLEY BALL TEAMS 
IN THE CITY LEAGUE, AN ACTIVE SWIMMING CLUB, HANDBALL, 
WITH OUR REGULAR GYMNASIUM CLASSES, COMBINED TO PROVIDE A 
VARIETY IN PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, TO BE FOUND IN NO OTHER ONE 
PLACE IN THIS CITY. WE CONDUCTED THE PROVINCIAL GYMNASTIC 


AND THE PROVINCIAL WRESTLING CHAMPIONSHIPS AGAIN THIS YEARe 


THE REGULAR PROGRAM OF THE BOYS’ DIVISION INCLUDED 
GYMNASIUM CLASSES, SWIMMING, VARIOUS INTEREST CLUBS AND 
CRAFT GROUPS, HIKES AND OUTINGS. THE BIBLE CLASS FOR OLDER 
BOYS, CONDUCTED BY MR. We MCLe CLARKE ON SUNDAY AFTERNOONS, 
HAD A VERY SUCCESSFUL SEASONe THE MOTHERS' CLUBS WERE OF 
GREAT ASSISTANCE ON MANY OCCASIONS, AND THEIR WORK 1S MUCH 
APPRECIATEDe 


BESIDES THE MORE THAN 600 BOYS IN OUR MEMBERSHIPP, 
THE BoYSt DIBISION HAS SERVED MANY NON-MEMBERS. OURING THE 
YEAR SOME 300 UNEMPLOYED B0YS USED OUR PRIVILEGES, INCLUDING 
GYM CLASSES, BOXING AND WRESTLING, LIBRARY, ETC. CLASSES IN 
SHORTHAND, FRENCH CONVERSATION, ENGLISH AND ARITHMETIC WERE 
CONDUCTED. THE LEATHER CRAFT GROUP, SPONSORED BY THE Y'S 
MEN'S CLUB, WAS AN ESPECIALLY WORTHWHILE VENTURE. 


ANOTHER IMPORTANT SERVICE TO BOYS OUTSIDE THE REGU- 
LAR MEMBERSHIP WAS THE ORGANIZATION OF FIVE CLUBS OF PICKED 
BOYS FROM THE ROYAL ARTHUR, WILLIAM LUNN, BERTHELET AND LEwis 
EVANS SCHOOLS, UNDER THE EFFECTIVE VOLUNTEER LEADERSHIP 
PROVIDED BY THE ASSOCIATION, THESE BOYS WERE CHALLENGED TO 
FINER CONDUCT IN THEIR SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY LIFE.

HON. HENRY MILESe 


IN CONNECTION WITH THE PASSING OF MRe DeA. BUDGE, 
THE ASSOCIATION HAS PAID THE FOLLOWING TRIBUTE TO HIS LIFE 
AND MEMORY. 


"RESOLVED": : 


"THAT THE MEMBERS OF THE METROPOLITAN BOARD OF DIR= 
ECTORS OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATION HAVE ‘LEARNED 
WITH PROFOUND REGRET OF THE DEATH ON FEBRUARY 13TH OF MRe 
DANIEL ANOREW BUDGE. 


? 
"MR. BUDGE WAS BORN IN 1851, THE YEAR IN WHICH’ THE 
FIRST ASSOCIATION IN NORTH AMERICA WAS FOUNDED IN MONTREAL es 
IN EARLY LIFE HE BECAME IDENTIFIED WITH THE ASSOCIATION 
MOVEMENT, MAINTAINING A CLOSE CONNECTION WITH, AND A HELP- 
FUL PARTICIPATION IN, tTS WORK UNTIL THE DAY OF HIS DEATHe 


WEOR THIRTY-NINE YEARS HE WAS THE HONOREO AND 
BELOVED SECRETARY OF THIS ASSOCIATION, SUBSEQUENTLY ACTING 
AS CONSULTING SECRETARY UNTIL HIS RETIREMENT IN 1922, THE 
RAPID GROWTH IN SERVICE AND INFLUENCE OF THE MONTREAL ASS- 
OCIATION 1S DUE EN A LARGE MEASURE TO HIS UNTIRING AND ~ 


AND DEVOTED EFFORTS, AND TO HIS WISE AND INSPIRING LEADER- 
SHIP.e HIS IDEALISM WAS CONTAGIOUS ANO HIS AIM IN LIFE WAS 
THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FINEST TYPE OF MANHOOD. 


"THROUGHOUT THE ENTIRE BROTHERHOOD, MR. BUDGE WAS 
WELL AND FAVORABLY KNOWN, AND HIS ADVICE AND COUNSEL WERE 
SOUGHT AND HIGHLY PRIZED. HIS CONTRIBUTION TO THE DEVELOP@ 
MENT OF THE ASSOCIATIONS IN CANADA, HIS RELATION TO THE WORK 
OF THEINTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE, AND HIS KEEN APPRECIATION OF 
AND HELPFUL ATTITUDE TO THE FOREIGN WORK ARE GRATEFULLY RE- 
CALLED. HIS SERVICES TO THE ASSOCIATIONS IN AUSTRALIA AND 
New ZEALAND, AND HIS SEVERAL VISITS TO GREAT BRITAIN BOTH 
BEFORE AND DURING THE GREAT WAR BROUGHT HIM IN HELPFUL RE- 


“LATIONSHIPS TO MANY OF THE OVERSEAS ASSOCIATIONS AND LEADERS. 


"HE IOENTIFIED HIMSELF WITH A WIDE RANGE OF ACTIVI- 
TIES IN THE INTERESTS OF THE SOCIAL AND RELIGIOUS WELFARE 
OF THE COMMUNITY IN WHICH HE LIVED, DEVOTING HIS EXPERIENCE 
AND TALENTS UNRESERVEOLY IN GIVING EFFECTIVE LEADERSHIP TO 
THE MANY FINANCIAL CAMPAIGNS FOR PHILANTHROPIC OBJECTS, 


"HIS COMPELLING PERSONALITY AND DEEPLY RELIGIOUS 
SPIRIT WON FOR HIM AN ABIDING PLACE IN THE HEARTS AND AFFECT- 
IONS OF LITTERALLY THOUSANDS OF YOUNG MEN WITH WHOM HE CAME 
IN CONTACT. THOUGH HIS VOICE IS NOW SILENT, HIS LIFE YET 
SPEAKS, HIS INFLUENCE STILL REMAINS, AND THE TRUE VALUE OF 
HIS LIFE'S SERVICE 1S INDELIBLY WRITTEN UPON THE HEARTS ANO 
LIVES OF MANY WHO GLADLY ACKNOWLEDGE HIS INSPIRING MINISTRA~- 
TIONS. A GREAT NUMBER OF THESE MEN HAVE PASSED ON, BUT WE, 
HIS MORE INTIMATE ASSOCIATES,WHOSEHEARTS HAVE BEEN KNIT WITH 
HIS «= WHILE WE REJOICE AT HIS ENTRANCE INTO THE PRESENCE OF 
HIM WHOM HE SERVED SO LONG AND SO FAITHFULLY -=- DESIRE TO 
EXPRESS OUR PROFOUND REGRET” AT THE PASSING OF A LIFE SO 
ABUNDANTLY FRUITFUL AND SO FULLY LIVED. 


"WE EXTEND TO THE MEMBERS OF HIS FAMILY OUR SINCERE 
SYMPATHY IN THE IRREPARABLE LOSS WHICH THEY HAVE SUSTAINED." 


IN THE DEATH OF LTe COLONEL HERBERT SNELL ON NOVEM~ 
BER 13TH, A MEMBER OF THE METROPOLITAN BOARD, THE FOLLOWING 
RESOLUTION WAS PLACED ON THE MINUTES OF THE BOARD OF DIRECT- 
ORS? 


"RESOLVED: 


"THAT THE MEMBERS OF THE METROPOLITAN BOARD OF THE 
MONTREAL YeMeCeAe LEARN WITH DEEP REGRET OF THE DEATH ON 
NOVEMBER 12TH, (932,. OF. LIEUTENANT@COLONEL HERBERT SNELLs 


"FOR MORE THAN TWENTY-FIVE YEARS, COLONEL SNELL 
AIDED AND ENRICHED THE LIFE OF THE ASSOCIATION IN ITS SERV- 
ICE TO THE YOUTH OF CANADA == FIRST IN MOOSEVAW, SASK., 
AND AS VICE-CHAIRMAN OF THE WESTERN DIVISION OF THE NATIONAL 
COUNCIL; SUBSEQUENTLY IN THE OVERSEAS MILITARY WORK OF THE 
YeleCeAe; AND, FINALLY, AS A MEMBER OF THE MONTREAL METRO- 
POLITAN BOARD. HIS OVERSEAS WORK WAS PECULIARLY VALUABLE 
IN THAT, COMMANDING A BATTALION,! HE YET FOUND TIME TO TAKE A 
PERSONAL INTEREST IN HIS MEN AND IN THE WORK OF THE ASSOCIA- 
TION FOR CANADIAN SOLDIERS IN ENGLAND AND FRANCE. AS 
CHAIRMAN OF THE MONTREAL CENTRAL BRANCH, AND AS VICE=CHAIR- 
MAN OF THE MONTREAL BUILDING COMMITTEE, HE GAVE UNSTINTINGLY 


OF HIS TIME, COUNSEL AND MEANS. THUS DURING THESE YEARS 
WHEN HIS LIFE WAS SWINGING TO ITS FULL CIRCLE, THIS ASS- 
OCIATION IN PARTICULAR, AND CANADIAN YOUTH IN GENERAL, 
BECAME INCREASINGLY DEBTOR TO COWONEL SNELL FOR HIS GEN- 
EROUS EXPENDITURE OF THESE FINE GIFTS OF MIND AND HEART 
THAT WERE PECULIARLY HIS OWN. CONSEQUENTLY HE MERITED AND 
RECEIVED THE FULLEST RESPECT AND ADMIRATION OF ALL WITH 
WHOM HE WORKEDe 


"THEREFORE THIS BOARD NOW RECORDS WITH, PROFOUND 
REGRET ITS SENSE OF ACUTE LOSS IN THE DEATH OF ONE OF ITS 
MOST LOYAL ANO DEVOTED MEMBERS." 


"BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT A COPY OF THIS RESOL- 
UTION BE FORWARDED TO MRS. SNELL WITH AN EXPRESSION OF 
THE BOARD'S SYMPATHY IN THE IRREPARABLE LOSS THAT SHE AND 
HER. FAMILY HAVE SUSTAINED." ; 


APPRECIATION: 


THERE ARE MANY FACTORS WHICH COMBINE TO MAKE 
POSSIBLE..A SUCCESSFUL YEAR'S WORK AN THE YeMeCeAe WE 
ARE GRATEFUL TO THE MANY FRIENDS WHO HAVE CONTRIBUTED 
GENEROUSLY OF THEIR FINANCIAL RESOURCES; TO THE WORKERS 
IN THE MAINTENANCE, AND OTHER CAMPAEGNS; TO MEMBERS OF 
BOARDS AND COMMITTEES FOR THEERFREQUENT COUNSEL, GUIDANCE 
AND SERVICE; TO THE MANY VOLUNTEERS WHO, HAVE SERVED AS | 
FRIENDLY COUNSELLORS OF CLUBS; JNTERVIEWERS; SPEAKERS; 
TEACHERS; INTERPRETERS; MINISTERS; TO THE PRESS; THE 
MEMBERS. OF THE LEADERS' CORPS; THE, STAFF; TO, THE CHURCHES; 
THE WOMEN'S AUXILIARIES; THE PROTESTANT BOARD OF SCHOOL 
COMMISSIONERS; RAILROAD AND OTHER CORPORATIONS; PARKS 
AND PLAYGROUND ASSOCIATION: THE YOUNG WOMEN'S CHRISTIAN 
ASSOCIATION, AND MANY OTHER CO-OPERATING AGENCIES. ABOVE 
ALL, WE ARE IN HUMILITY GRATEFUL TO GOD FOR HIS BLESSING 
AND. POWER. 


CONCLUSION: 


IN CLOSING THIS IMPERFECT RECORD OF A STRENUOUS 
YEAR'S WORK IN OUR GREAT METROPOLITAN CITY, MAY WE RE= 
MIND OURSELVES THAT THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIA= 
TION IN ITS ESSENTIAL GENIUS IS A WORLD-WIDE FELLOWSHIP 
OF MEN AND BOYS UNITED BY A “COMMON LOYALTY TO JESUS 
CHRIST FOR THE PURPOSE OF BUILDING CHRISTIAN PERSONALETY 
AND A CHRISTIAN SOCHETYe THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THIS OBJECT- 
IVE GAN PERHAPS BE MORE CLEARLY UNDERSTOOD. IN THE LIGHT 
OF THE FOLLOWING MEDITATION BY DR» LePe JACKS: 


"1T WOULD SEEM THAT- RELIGION ALWAYS CAME TO THE 
OUTSTANDING RELIGIOUS FIGURES OF HISTORY, NOT WHEN THEY 
WERE STUDYING RELIGION, BUT WHEN THEY WERE STUDYING SOME-~ 
THING ELSE; NEVER CAME AS THE THING THEY WERE DIRECTLY 
AIMING AT, BUT ALWAYS AS THE RESULT, SOMETIMES UNEXPECT~- 
ED, OF THEIR GETTING DEEPLY IMMERSED IN OTHER THINGS; 
DEEPLY IMMERSED IN THE WORK OF THEIR HANDS AS HUNTERS, 
SHEPHERDS, MARINERS, TILLERS OF THE SOIL, OR AS ARTISTS 
AND CRAFTSMEN; DEEPLY IMMERSED IN THE JOYS AND SORROWS 
OF THEIR. NEIGHBORS; DEEPLY IMMERSED IN THE DUTIES ANDO 
RESPONSIBILITIES OF THEIR CITIZENSHIP; DEEPLY IMMERSED 
IN THE STRUGGLE FOR EXISTENCE, THE BATTLE OF LIFE. OUT 


cal 


_OF THESE DEEP IMMERSIONS THERE CAME RELIGION, CAME SPONT- 
“ ANEOUSLY WITHOUT BEING SOUGHT FOR OR WORRIED ABOUT, CAME, 
AS IT WERE, BY INDIRECTIONe SUCH SEEMS TO HAVE BEEN THE 
WAY §#N WHICH RELIGION WAS BORN IN THE GREAT MEN OF OLD, 
NOT BY TAKING IT VIGOROUSLY IN HAND, BUT BY TAKING SOME- 
THING ELSE VIGOROUSLY IN HAND. ONE MIGHT DESCRIBE RELIG- 
10ON AS A BYPRODUCT OF THE PURSUIT OF EXCELLENCE, BUT 
OBVIOUSLY OF GREAT VALUE.” 


THE WORK OF THE YeMeCeAe IN THE YEAR JUST CLOSED 
HAS BEEN TRULY IN THE PURSUIT OF EXCELLENCE IN INDIVIDUAL 
LIVES AND IN SOCIETY. 


RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED, 


J.W. BEATON 


GENERAL SECRETARY.
